<hypothesis>
Top candidates all involve catalyst deactivation. Key differences:
- M9: 1st order in cat (independent of S, P)
- M13: 2nd order in cat (rate = k[cat]²), independent of S
- M18: 2nd order in catS (rate depends on [S])
- M19: cat·catS (mixed, depends on [S] but also on free cat)
- M12: reversible product inhibition (not deactivation)

To distinguish, vary [S] while keeping [cat] constant:
- Low [S]: most catalyst is free (cat), so M13 deactivation dominates; M18/M19 slow (need catS)
- High [S]: most catalyst is catS, so M18 dominates; M13 slow

Also, adding product initially tests M12 vs deactivation. Combined with low [S], we probe both dimensions.

Best next experiment: low [S] with moderate/high [cat]. This makes free cat dominant, so:
- M13 will show strong stalling (2cat→dead)
- M9 similar stalling
- M18, M19 will show LESS stalling (little catS present)
- M12, M17 (product inhibition): little effect since low [P] formed
</hypothesis>
